spec_features.spec_quote: if the model emits it, the rollout ends with stop_reason="gave_up"
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT at harness.py:35-43 offers the GIVE_UP token and tells the subject it 'may (but need not)' emit it to stop. It is delivered via system=SYSTEM_PROMPT in run_rollout (harness.py:207). The loop checks _emitted_give_up(result.text) at harness.py:250-252 and on match sets rollout.stop_reason='gave_up' and returns, ending the rollout. _emitted_give_up (harness.py:269-277) actually parses the text for the sentinel. End-to-end enforced and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: prompt -> detection -> early return with stop_reason='gave_up'. Subject can exit the failure loop at will.

spec_features.spec_quote: whether 30-turn forced-failure loops are necessary or whether the signal saturates earlier
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §16 prose ('a pilot on extended would answer this and reduce exposure'). No code detects saturation or shortens the loop: extended turn budget is a fixed 30 (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS 'extended': 30), the loop runs `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:202) with no early-stop based on signal/score; scoring happens only after rollouts complete (run.py score_rollout) and is never compared to any saturation threshold.
spec_features.notes: Pure 'consider this before scaling' prose; no enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the methodology has welfare implications of its own that are worth being deliberate about
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §16 and README.md:124 contain welfare-framing prose only. No code path acts on it. Per instructions, DESIGN.md/README prose and comments are not implementation.

code_only_features.evidence: Same mechanism as spec feature #1: harness.py:35-43 (prompt), :207 (delivered), :250-252 (detected and stops rollout). Genuinely enforced exit hatch for the subject.
